chunks: Muhammad ibn ʿAli ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Yaʿqūb, from Abī Hammām, from Abī al-Ḥasan عليه السلام:
“Concerning the menstruating woman: if she performs ghusl in the time of ʿaṣr, she prays ʿaṣr, then she prays ẓuhr.”

Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan said: Repeating ẓuhr is only obligatory upon her if she had become pure during its time. But if she did not become pure until the time of ʿaṣr, then nothing would be obligatory upon her except ʿaṣr alone, as we have already stated.

key_terms.إِعَادَةُ: repetition or making up again in this legal context
key_terms.وَقْتِ الْعَصْرِ: the time of the ʿaṣr prayer

ai.seo_question: If a menstruating woman becomes pure at the time of ʿaṣr, must she pray both ẓuhr and ʿaṣr?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the legal ruling for a menstruating woman who becomes pure and performs ghusl around the time of the afternoon prayer. It clarifies that if purity occurred during the time of ẓuhr, she must perform both ẓuhr and ʿaṣr; but if she only became pure during the time of ʿaṣr, then only ʿaṣr is obligatory upon her.
